answer: Each agent must lock a nontransferable bond in a vault before it can submit claims; a trellis of randomly assigned tasks then checks whether its outputs agree with independent agents and later evidence. Repeated identities controlled by one attacker are more likely to collide in the same review groups, exposing coordinated answers. Proven fraud burns the bond and bars the operator’s stake for a period, so creating many sybils multiplies capital at risk rather than earning free influence. Even shale-branded accounts must pay that cost.
